Let G be a finite abelian group and π : π 1 ( M -L ) → G be a surjective homomorphism. Let M π → M denote the branched cover corresponding to π , that is, the Fox completion of the unbranched covering corresponding to ker π . Then the transformation group of M π → M is G . 4.2. Z d p -coverings. Let π : π 1 ( M -L ) → Z d p be the composition map of the abelianization π 1 ( M -L ) → π 1 ( M -L ) ab ( ∼ = Z d ) and the inclusion Z d ↪ → Z d p . For a finite index subgroup Γ ⊂ Z d p let π Γ : π 1 ( M -L ) → Z d p / Γ denote the composition of π and the canonical surjective map Z d p → Z d p / Γ. Let M Γ → M denote the branched covering of ( M,L ) corresponding to π Γ .

Definition 4.2. A branched Z d p -covering of ( M,L ) is the inverse system of branched coverings M Γ → M where Γ runs finite index open subgroups in Z d p .

We obtain the p -adic convergence of the nonp -parts of the sizes of the first homology groups in branched Z d p -covering of ( M,L ). For a Z p -module A let rank A = dim F p A ⊗ F p .

Lemma 4.3. Let Γ 1 ⊃ Γ 2 ⊃ · · · be a descending sequence of finite open subgroups such that ∩ n Γ n = { 0 } in Z d p . Then we have

- (1) for all sufficiently large n , rank Z d p / Γ n = d .
- (2) for each meridian m of L , lim n →∞ ord( π Γ n ( m )) = ∞ .

Proof. We put G n = Z d p / Γ n .

(1) We note that lim ← -n G n ∼ = Z d p by the assumption ∩ n Γ n = { 0 } . Since the canonical homomorphisms F n : Z d p → G n and f n/n -1 : G n → G n -1 are surjective the induced homomorphisms ˜ F n : Z d p ⊗ F p → G n ⊗ F p and ˜ f n/n -1 : G n ⊗ F p → G n -1 ⊗ F p are also surjective. Thus we have that the sequence (rank G n ) is monotonically increasing. We suppose that rank G n < d for all n > 0. Then we have that dim F p ker ˜ F n ≥ 1 for all n . Since ker ˜ F n ⊂ ker ˜ F n -1 for all n > 1, we see that dim F n ∩ n ker ˜ F n ≥ 1. Thus
